cf0b801997ff4d24d977308ec1cd6b309d21e94b.text:
{
  "notes": [
    "Real GDP expanded by 7.1 percent in 2024 and 7.5 percent (y/y) in H1 2025, with projected growth slowing to 6.5 percent in 2025 and 5.6 percent in 2026.",
    "Credit to the economy grew by 14.9 percent in 2024, with projections of 15.0 percent in 2025 and 13.0 percent in 2026.",
    "Broad money (M2) growth was 12.0 percent in 2024, and is projected to reach 12.5 percent in 2025 and 11.5 percent in 2026.",
    "Domestic macro-financial risks include potential financial stress from tighter financial conditions and high corporate indebtedness.",
    "Priority actions for financial sector stability include building liquidity and capital buffers and improving the macroprudential toolkit.",
    "Space for monetary policy easing is very limited, requiring close monitoring of inflation and FX risks alongside greater exchange rate flexibility.",
    "Directors recommended further upgrading of crisis preparedness and resolution, insolvency, AML/CFT frameworks, and the regulation of crypto assets."
  ],
  "summary": "Vietnam’s economy grew by 7.1 percent in 2024 and 7.5 percent (y/y) in H1 2025, supported by export momentum and credit growth. However, growth is projected to decelerate to 6.5 percent in 2025 and 5.6 percent in 2026 amid global trade uncertainty and domestic risks from high corporate indebtedness. With monetary policy space limited, recommendations emphasize exchange rate flexibility, building bank capital and liquidity buffers, upgrading macroprudential and resolution frameworks, and using fiscal policy prudently to support activity."
}

593c33f511f7c4b3ea8c184ca125814fd82aafe4.text:
{
  "notes": [
    "2025:H1 GDP growth accelerated to 7.5 percent y/y, driven by accommodative policies, export front-loading, and temporary government spending.",
    "Headline inflation reached 3.6 percent in June 2025, staying beneath the official 41⁄2-5 percent target range.",
    "The 2024 current account surplus rose to a historical high of 6.6 percent of GDP, accompanied by high errors and omissions of 6.9 percent of GDP.",
    "The Vietnamese dong depreciated 5 percent against the U.S. dollar in 2024 and continued to weaken in 2025, prompting the SBV to adjust the center of its ±5-percent exchange rate band.",
    "Bank credit growth expanded significantly to 15 percent in 2024 and 19 percent y/y in June 2025, raising the credit stock to 136 percent of GDP with a positive credit-to-GDP gap.",
    "Financial system risks remain in the corporate bond market due to a concentration of maturities due in 2025:H2 and an interconnected, institution-dominated investor base.",
    "The 2024 fiscal deficit was estimated at 1.5 percent of GDP, with public and publicly guaranteed debt standing at 31.3 percent of GDP.",
    "Trade risks are elevated due to new U.S. tariffs expected to reach 20 percent from August, alongside a 40 percent tariff rate on transshipments."
  ],
  "summary": "Vietnam’s economy grew 7.5 percent y/y in 2025:H1, supported by accommodative policies, front-loaded exports, and rapid credit growth (19 percent y/y in June 2025). June inflation reached 3.6 percent, remaining below the 41⁄2-5 percent target. The 2024 current account surplus reached 6.6 percent of GDP, while total credit reached 136 percent of GDP. Financial risks persist from exchange rate depreciation—following a 5 percent decline against the U.S. dollar in 2024—impending U.S. tariffs up to 20–40 percent, and substantial corporate bond maturities in 2025:H2."
}

{
  "notes": [
    "The on-balance-sheet non-performing loan (NPL) ratio declined from a peak of 5.9 percent in September 2023 to 5.3 percent in March 2025, but remains above the 2.3 percent level in 2022.",
    "Capital adequacy ratios reached 10.4 percent for public banks and 12.1 percent for private banks in 2024:Q1, while liquid assets accounted for only 7.8 percent of total assets as of June 2024.",
    "The banking system loan-to-deposit ratio exceeds 100 percent, increasing reliance on wholesale funding amid elevated corporate vulnerabilities in the real estate sector.",

    "Early retirement packages for institutional restructuring are estimated to cost 1 percent of GDP during 2025-26, with expected wage bill savings of 0.9 percent of GDP annually.",
    "Public investment implementation reached 91 percent of the plan in 2024; model simulations show scaling up public investment by 11.5 percent of GDP over 2025-30 could raise medium-term growth by more than 2 percentage points.",
    "Replacing the current debt ceiling of 60 percent of GDP with a lower ceiling of 50 percent of GDP is recommended as a prudent medium-term anchor.",
    "The foreign direct investment (FDI) sector accounted for almost 40 percent of firms' employment in 2022 and over 70 percent of exports in 2024, emphasizing dualism relative to domestic firms."
  ],
  "summary": "In 2025, Vietnam faces elevated global trade uncertainty, requiring flexible policy responses. The fiscal deficit is projected to widen to 3.3 percent of GDP in 2025 before narrowing to 2.3 percent in 2026. Financial sector vulnerabilities remain elevated: the NPL ratio stood at 5.3 percent in March 2025, the loan-to-deposit ratio exceeds 100 percent, and liquid assets were just 7.8 percent of total assets as of June 2024. Scaling up public investment by 11.5 percent of GDP over 2025-30 could raise medium-term growth by over 2 percentage points."
}

dc7fad41fff9021e5d1720fdd06963f9f6b97404.text: The context indicates that IMF capacity development and technical assistance in the financial sector focus on stress testing, digital bank regulation, consolidated supervision, and addressing AML/CFT deficiencies [chunk 76]. Additionally, the IMF emphasizes that strengthening the resilience of the financial sector will be important [chunk 1]. However, the provided context does not contain specific recommendations regarding bank provisioning or broader banking supervision policies.

406b2bb5596c17f5f2d9e41ef66c5988bc1cf82d.text: Vietnam's inflation is projected to remain stable below the 4.5–5 percent target in 2025 and fall in 2026 as a negative output gap opens [chunk 16]. While headline inflation has been contained by lower fuel prices and administered prices, core inflation has risen due to increasing housing costs and strong credit growth [chunk 46, chunk 20]. Other key drivers influencing these trends include disinflationary spillovers from China, exchange rate pressures, and wage increases supported by a strong labor market [chunk 16, chunk 20, chunk 46].

738d42371881a0102132ea04f7bd220c057df41e.text: Not found in the retrieved context.

25f8e7be39c2f359769ed21a3ec549c0fa23bad4.text: Changing and uncertain global trade policies pose a persistent drag on investment, potential medium-term growth, and trade operations in Vietnam [chunk 17, chunk 87]. Higher tariffs and stringent rules of origin could disrupt exports, lower economic growth by an additional 0.2–0.6 percentage points under a downside scenario, and reduce FDI and other financial inflows [chunk 17, chunk 87]. Furthermore, these developments could increase exchange rate pressures, generate negative spillovers to the domestic economy and banking system, hurt business sentiment, and disrupt supply chains [chunk 87].

2ff842eea04986bcaaf969f546c3cce890f6fff5.text: Bank credit growth accelerated to 15 percent in 2024 and 19 percent year-over-year in June 2025, raising total credit to 136 percent of GDP with a positive credit-to-GDP gap [chunk 15] (with year-to-date credit growth reaching 8.30 percent by end-June 2025 [chunk 103]). This high credit expansion creates financial stability risks, including potential distress among real estate developers, asset quality deterioration, liquidity squeezes at weak banks, and corporate/household balance sheet stress from debt overhang [chunk 79]. Furthermore, rapid credit growth combined with thin bank capital buffers risks lowering credit standards and making the banking system more vulnerable to economic shocks [chunk 88].

049b2271000b59a2a107d8be840d2fd9a2fc2706.text: The IMF highlights vulnerabilities in the corporate bond market due to a large volume of maturities coming due in the second half of 2025, alongside a limited and interconnected investor base consisting mostly of financial institutions [chunk 15]. Additionally, underlying distress among real estate developers remains an ongoing concern that could re-intensify if economic growth slows sharply from trade shocks, threatening to amplify credit risks and adversely impact banks [chunk 79].

6a68bd35d7527e1206a9cb1c85e8ba83aed5f08d.text: According to the report's Financial Soundness Indicators, the Regulatory Tier 1 Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets ratio for Vietnamese banks was 9.5 percent in 2020, 9.6 percent in 2021, 10.1 percent in 2022, and 10.4 percent in 2023 [chunk 71]. By the second quarter of 2024, the Tier 1 capital ratio reached 10.6 percent [chunk 71].

db91e6d0b46c1a655d36de6355aac29fd0a2de09.text: The IMF recommends bolstering capital-based macroprudential tools to build larger capital and liquidity buffers in banks, providing a more efficient alternative to aggregate credit ceilings [chunk 88]. Additionally, recommendations include strengthening systemic risk assessments, monitoring the impact of trade shocks on banks, accelerating the AML/CFT framework, and advancing crypto asset regulations [chunk 31]. b36f6ee92ba3f471582392d9cc24c35b1777e919.text: Vietnam's inflation is projected to remain stable below the 4.5-5% target in 2025 and fall in 2026 as a negative output gap opens [chunk 16, chunk 103]. Period average CPI is expected to be 3.4% in 2025 and 3.2% in 2026, while core inflation is projected to reach 3.2% in 2025 before declining to 2.8% in 2026 [chunk 59]. Key drivers include domestic economic activity, exchange rate pressures, and rising housing costs, which are currently being offset by disinflation in fuel prices and low inflation in China [chunk 16, chunk 20, chunk 46]. Additionally, a strong labor market and the 2024 public wage hike have supported wage increases, influencing the inflationary environment [chunk 46].

cc30e01efefa6dad847000458e1e88bb70e46695.text: Changes in global trade policy and heightened uncertainty pose risks by placing a persistent drag on investment, depressing external demand and FDI, and constraining economic growth [chunk 17, chunk 87, chunk 15]. Higher tariffs applied directly or through global value chains can disrupt exports, increase exchange rate pressures, cause temporary supply shortages, limit job creation, and depress business sentiment [chunk 17, chunk 87, chunk 86]. Additionally, weaker profitability and liquidity in the exporting FDI sector could create negative spillovers into the domestic economy and banking system [chunk 87].

cfef4249a50bf3a1afbda5bee3d56242a72a9569.text: Bank credit growth accelerated to 15 percent in 2024 and reached 19 percent year-over-year in June 2025 [chunk 14, chunk 15]. This rapid expansion raised the total stock of credit to 136 percent of GDP—exceeding most emerging markets—with the credit-to-GDP gap remaining positive in 2024 [chunk 15]. Key financial risks include squeezed profit margins for banks [chunk 51] as well as corporate bond market vulnerabilities driven by a large bulk of maturities coming due in 2025:H2 and a limited, interconnected investor base consisting mostly of financial institutions [chunk 15].

dd4e5685bd02a6f6a7aacc903888b0bcacfeb25e.text: Real estate developers face ongoing distress that could re-intensify if economic growth slows, potentially leading to liquidity squeezes and asset quality concerns at weak banks [chunk 79]. The corporate bond market is vulnerable due to a large volume of maturities scheduled for the second half of 2025 and a limited, interconnected investor base dominated by financial institutions [chunk 15, chunk 55]. Additionally, the IMF identifies risks from corporate debt overhangs and liquidity constraints that could propagate balance sheet stress [chunk 79].

07ac8c78b76818ec8a76f771b9c1966024fdfe12.text: As of the second quarter of 2024, the regulatory Tier 1 capital to risk-weighted assets for Vietnamese banks was 10.6 percent [chunk 71]. This ratio has shown a steady increase over recent years, rising from 9.5 percent in 2020 to 10.4 percent in 2023 [chunk 71]. Despite these improvements, Vietnamese banks generally apply Basel II standards, which utilize a less stringent definition of capital than Basel III and offer less shock absorption capacity [chunk 88].
